Give upkeep a reason

By v/hNovember 18, 2026Visual note

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

A maintenance reminder creates a task for the owner. It should have a reason.

Imagine a device that asks for cleaning after a fixed number of uses. A light task and a messy task add the same count, even when they leave a part in different conditions.

Where the condition can be checked reliably, we would want the device to use that evidence. Where it cannot, the message should ask the owner to inspect a named part rather than claim a fault.

A local agent could compare current inputs with feedback from the job. Any request for help should have an instruction the owner can follow on the object itself.

During development, we would compare reminders with direct inspections. Count both unnecessary cleaning requests and missed cleaning needs, then check whether the advised action restores readiness.

Our first utility is in development. The example and graphic illustrate a proposed upkeep requirement.
